info.title: Kaeso Platform API
info.description: Manage a Kaeso install: organizations, projects, members, keys, provider credentials, models, limits, usage and logs. Every operation names the single right it checks. Errors are `{"error": {"type", "message", "param"}}`. Lists are paginated with `limit` and `after`.

post.summary: Updates the install to the newest offered release through the updater, with a recent sign-in; the console and the APIs are unavailable for about a minute.
post.description:
The updater checks the release's signed provenance, downloads the images, switches the console and then the gateway, and waits for the gateway's migrations and health. When the new version fails it goes back to the previous one, unless the new gateway may already have migrated the database: then it leaves the new gateway in place and ends `needs_attention`. Poll `instance/updates/jobs/{update}` for the progress; when the updater doesn't confirm the start, the update stays `running` until the updater reports on it.

**Access:** a console session of an instance admin.

The org: from its sign-in link (`/sign-in?org=…`, the `sign_in_url` of
its SSO connection), from `provider` in `auth/methods`, or from the
console page that asks for its SSO.

estimated_disk_bytes.description:
Estimated size on disk: metadata rows at the table's average row size,
plus content at its current compression ratio.

StreamProgressView.description: How far a streamed reply got.

bytes.description: Bytes written to the app, keepalives included.

events.description: Stream events decoded from the provider.

first_byte_ms.description:
Time from the request's arrival to the first reply bytes written to
the app, in milliseconds; `null` when none were.

keepalives.description:
Keepalives the gateway wrote because the app had seen nothing for the
keepalive interval.

log_buffer.description: Request log rows waiting for ClickHouse on this instance.

TestEmail.description: Where to send a test email.

TestEmailResult.description: The outcome of a test email.

TokenPrice.description:
USD per million tokens, from 0 to 1,000,000 with at most 9 decimals, sent as a
decimal string, such as `"2.50"`, or as a whole JSON number; a fraction sent as a
JSON number is refused.

TotpConfirm.description: The first code from the authenticator app.

recovery_codes.description: Ten one-time recovery codes. Shown once; store them safely.

TotpRequest.description: The second step of a password sign-in.

code.description: A 6-digit code from the authenticator app.

recovery_code.description: Or one of the recovery codes (each works once).

challenge.description: Pass to `auth/totp` with a code. Valid for 5 minutes.

TotpSetup.description: A TOTP secret waiting for its first code.

otpauth_uri.description: The `otpauth://` URI, for a QR code.

secret.description: The secret in base32, to type into an authenticator app.

UpdateCheckView.description: The last look for new releases.

error.description: Why the last look failed, if it did.

last_success_at.description: When the gateway last got the list of releases.

next_check_at.description: When it looks next, while checking is on.

UpdateJobView.description: An update of the install from one version to another.

automatic.description: Whether the gateway started it by itself in the update window.

detail.description: The updater's account of what went wrong, in English.

finished_at.description: When it ended; `null` while it runs.

reason.description: Why it did not succeed, or what is left to do after it did, as a code: `manifest_unavailable`, `manifest_invalid`, `manual_steps`, `major`, `not_newer`, `updater_outdated`, `compose_changed`, `compose_unwritable`, `services_not_found`, `pull_failed`, `unverified`, `docker_unavailable`, `unhealthy`, `interrupted`, `updater_unreachable`, `updater_refused`, `state_unwritable` or `migrated` (the new gateway didn't start and may have migrated the database).

oneOf.description: Who started it; `null` when the gateway started it in the update window or once that user is deleted.

state.description: `running`, `succeeded` (with a `reason` when compose.yaml still needs the new version by hand), `failed` (nothing changed), `rolled_back` (the previous version runs again), `rollback_failed` (the previous version did not start again) or `needs_attention` (the new gateway may have migrated the database and did not start; someone has to look).

step.description: The step it is on or ended on: `verifying`, `downloading`, `switching`, `migrating` or `online`.

UpdateMode.description: How the install takes updates through the updater.

frequency.description: Every day or once a week.

hour.description: The hour the update window opens, 0 to 23, in the instance's time zone.

weekday.description: The day of a weekly update; ignored for a daily one.

timezone.description: The instance's IANA time zone, which the hour follows, daylight saving time included; set in the instance settings.

weekday.description: The day of a weekly update.

oneOf.description: Which releases are offered.
`manual` or `automatic`; choosing `automatic` needs a recent sign-in.
When automatic updates run.

check.description: Whether the gateway looks for new releases twice a day; `updates.check` in the configuration turns it off for installs without internet.

mode.description: `manual` (an instance admin starts each update) or `automatic` (the gateway installs new releases in the update window).

next_auto_update_at.description: When the next update window opens, while automatic updates are on.

UpdaterView.description: The updater, the optional service that applies updates.

state.description: `not_installed` (no updater token is set), `unreachable` (it does not answer, or cannot reach Docker), `outdated` (too old for the newest release) or `ready`.

UpdatesView.description: Updates of the install: the running version, newer releases, the settings, the updater and the last update.

can_apply.description: Whether the newest release can be applied now: nothing asks for steps by hand, the updater is ready and no update runs.

oneOf.description: The running update, or else the last one.
The newest offered release, when it is newer than the running version.

manual.description: Why the updater can't install the newest release: `major` (a new major version), `manual_steps` (a release on the way asks for steps by hand) or `not_prepared` (it has no release manifest); `null` when it can.

releases.description: Every offered release newer than the running version, newest first.

state.description: `unknown` until the gateway first gets the list of releases, `up_to_date`, or `available` when a newer release is offered.

upgrade_guide.description: The guide to updating by hand.

cost.description: Cost in USD; `null` without the right to see costs.

errors.description:
Of those, the ones answered with a status of 400 or above, the
gateway's own refusals and streams that failed after their headers
included.

key.description:
The day, the Monday of the week, the first day of the month,
`provider/model`, key id (`playground` for the requests members made
in the console's Playground, without a key), member (`user:<id>` or
`service_account:<id>`), or project id.

requests.description:
Model requests of the group, made with a key or from the Playground:
every one, the gateway's own refusals (limits, unknown models,
capability checks) included.

first_day.description:
The first day with usage (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD`); `null` before the first
request. "All time" starts here.

last_day.description: The last day with usage (UTC); `null` before the first request.

estimated.description:
Whether these counts are partly estimated: the stream ended (the app
went away, or the provider's stream broke off) before the provider
reported its final usage. Input then comes from the provider's
report at the start of the stream or its token-counting endpoint
(else about 4 bytes of the request per token), output from the
content received (at least one token per delta and per 4 bytes).
Costs and limits use the same numbers.

UserLocale.description: The language a person reads the console in.

UserView.description: A user as the user and their org admins see them.

avatar_url.description: The picture's address, under `me/avatars`; `null` without one.

email.description: The email address; `null` for a deleted user.

is_instance_admin.description: Whether the user administers the whole install.

name.description: The display name; `"Deleted user"` for a deleted user.

WhatsNewRelease.description: A Kaeso release the signed-in user hasn't seen yet.

oneOf.description: The release's artwork as update.kaeso.app chose it once for good; `null` when the feed has none, and the console then draws one from the version.

notes.description: The release notes, in Markdown; empty when the gateway doesn't know them.

published_at.description: When it was published; `null` when the gateway doesn't know the release list.

WhatsNewView.description: What changed in Kaeso since the signed-in user last saw it.

releases.description: Every release after `seen` up to the running version, newest first, at most 10; pre-releases only while a pre-release runs.

seen.description: The last version the user saw; `null` for someone who never signed in to the console before, who has nothing new to see.

can_create_orgs.description:
Whether the user may create organizations (`POST me/orgs`): always
for instance admins; for everyone else as the instance setting
`org_creation` says, by their email domain when it is
`allowed_domains`.

locale.description:
The language the console is shown in, as in `me`:
the console reads it at start, before anything else is shown.

org_deletion.description:
Whether orgs can be deleted on this instance, and how long a deletion
waits.

timezone.description: The install's IANA time zone: the console shows every time in it.

totp_enabled.description: Whether the user has confirmed TOTP.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state (`conflict`).

Forbidden.description: The caller lacks the right, the org requires 2FA or SSO, or a recent sign-in is needed (`permission_denied`, `recent_sign_in_required`).

Internal.description: An unexpected error; the message names the request id (`internal`).

InvalidRequest.description: The request is malformed or a value is invalid (`invalid_request`).

api_key.description: An API key with platform access (`sk-kso-…`, acting as its principal inside its project) or an org platform key (`sk-kso-org-…`).
